drivers.theme: Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2025 (Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha)
drivers.detail: Passed Dec-2025: FDI cap 74% -> 100%; stronger IRDAI enforcement powers; foreign reinsurer NOF Rs 5,000 cr -> 1,000 cr. Composite licences and lower minimum capital for insurers were NOT included. More foreign capital/entrants (Bajaj bought out Allianz Mar-2026; Liberty Mutual to 74%) -> more competition.
drivers.note: Mixed: capital availability positive; competitive intensity negative for incumbents. Exclusions: https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/india-s-parliament-approves-bill-to-raise-foreign-direct-investment-in-insurance-to-100-ce7d50dfdc8cf325

drivers.detail: From 1-Oct-2024 multi-year premiums recognised 1/n per year in GDPI; cut FY25 reported growth to 6.2% (8.6% ex-1/n) and FY26 to ~9.3% (11.1% ex-1/n per ICRA). Base effect largely washed out by FY27.
drivers.note: Reporting headwind FY25-26; neutral/tailwind (cleaner comps) from FY27

drivers.theme: IRDAI EoM regulations & proposed distribution overhaul
drivers.detail: IRDAI consultation (23-Sep-2026) 'Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution': 30+ product/channel commission caps, ~one-third cut in overall EoM limits, three-tier distribution, clawbacks; proposed effective 1-Jan-2027; IBAI opposes, IRDAI may extend timeline.
drivers.note: For Go Digit (broker/POSP-heavy motor): growth/channel disruption risk, but lower commissions could improve COR

drivers.detail: No TP tariff hike since June-2022; IRDAI proposed ~18% avg (up to 25%) in 2025; as of Jul-2026 insurers still seeking a hike - not notified. ICRA flags TP revision as upside to growth and underwriting.
drivers.note: A hike would be a tailwind (optionality). Jul-2026 status per secondary report: https://india-employmentnews.com/utility-news/insurance-premium-hike-third-party-insurance-for-cars-and/cid19048304.htm

drivers.theme: Ind AS 117 / IFRS 17 and risk-based capital (RBC)
drivers.detail: IRDAI exposure draft (Mar-2026) proposes Ind AS (incl. Ind AS 117) for all insurers from 1-Apr-2026 with parallel IGAAP regulatory reporting and a one-year forbearance option; listed insurers already disclose Ind AS/IFRS metrics. RBC approved in principle; go-live date unconfirmed (likely post-2027).
drivers.note: Better comparability and capital efficiency; near-term reporting noise (CareEdge)

drivers.detail: IRDAI digital marketplace; info hub launched Sep-2025; transactional launch repeatedly delayed, now targeted ~Nov-2026 (motor, health, term first). Could lower acquisition costs but commoditise motor pricing.
drivers.note: Mixed for digital-first players like Go Digit

drivers.detail: IRDAI vision; India non-life penetration ~1% of GDP (density US$25) vs world 4.3%/US$555 - long runway; push via Bima Trinity, state champions, simplified products.
drivers.note: Penetration has been flat at ~0.9-1.0% for a decade despite the push

drivers.theme: GST 2.0: individual health & life premiums exempt (from 22-Sep-2025)
drivers.detail: 18% -> 0% on individual health/life: retail health +19.9% FY26 and ~+33% H1 FY27; SAHIs +30.7% H1 FY27. Insurers lost input tax credit on exempt lines - partly passed to distributors (ICICI Lombard cut commissions ~18% on exempt policies). Group health/motor still taxed. Go Digit is motor-heavy, so benefits less directly.

SAHI UW losses +63% in FY26; regulator scrutiny of claim rejections and cashless; proposed 10% co-pay on retail claims may not get IRDAI nod; GST-led shift to higher sums insured raises claims exposure.
PV domestic sales Apr-Sep 2026 +28.3% (Q2 FY27 +30.7%); all vehicles +19.8% (SIAM). Motor GDPI +12.9% in Sep-2026; renewal-heavy books dilute pass-through (BCG: FY26 auto +10.4% vs motor +9.2%).
drivers.note: Directly positive for motor-heavy Go Digit

drivers.detail: Swiss Re: EV penetration is the most prominent premium-supportive force in motor (higher repair costs/sums insured); IRDAI permits pay-as/how-you-drive add-ons under Use & File, favouring telematics/digital players.
Crop GDPI -36% FY26 and ~-31% H1 FY27 on aggressive pricing/lower state participation; commercial fire/engineering renewals heavily discounted; global P&C soft market 2026-27 (Swiss Re).
drivers.note: Drags industry growth; limited direct Go Digit exposure

drivers.theme: PSU weakness / share shift to private
drivers.detail: PSU share (incl. AIC/ECGC) fell from 42.8% (FY21) to 34.0% (FY26); PSU multiline UW loss Rs 29,071 cr in FY26 (wage revision); three of four PSUs loss-making and below 1.5x solvency except New India (BCG).
drivers.note: Supports private share gains, though PSU pricing in group health/commercial remains aggressive

porter.rivalry: High: ~35 insurers; motor and group health price-competitive, PSUs price below cost, new SAHIs and 100% FDI add capacity; industry COR ~113% (FY26).
porter.threatOfNewEntrants: Medium-high: 100% FDI and new licences (Galaxy, Narayana, Kshema) lower barriers, but Rs 100 cr minimum capital, 1.5x solvency, distribution and claims infrastructure still bind.
porter.buyerPower: High in motor/group/commercial (brokers, OEM dealers, corporates, aggregators; Bima Sugam adds price transparency); lower in retail health (agency-led, sticky renewals).
porter.supplierPower: Medium-high: distributors (brokers, banks, OEMs, POSPs) take ~15% of NEP in commission; hospitals have pricing power in health claims; reinsurers (GIC Re via obligatory cession) set cat-line terms.
porter.threatOfSubstitutes: Low: motor TP is mandatory; substitutes are self-insurance, government schemes (PM-JAY crowds out low-end health) and employer group cover.

themes: Health is the growth engine: ~41% of GDPI in FY26, retail health growing 20-30%+ post GST exemption; SAHIs gaining share (7.9% FY21 -> 13.7% FY26, ~14% H1 FY27), but loss ratios and medical inflation are the swing factor.
Motor volume up-cycle in FY27 (PV +28% H1) with optionality from a long-delayed TP tariff hike (none since Jun-2022); EVs and telematics/use-based products reshape motor pricing - key for Go Digit.

Distribution economics reset: IRDAI's proposed commission caps and ~1/3 EoM cut (from Jan-2027) would compress acquisition costs and broker/POSP payouts - positive for COR, disruptive for broker-led growth.

Underwriting losses are structural (industry COR 111-113%, UW loss Rs 45k cr FY26); returns depend on investment income (~Rs 48k cr FY25), so yields/MTM drive ROE; disciplined large privates earn 15-18% ROE vs ~6% for the industry.
Private share gains continue as PSUs (34% incl. AIC/ECGC) struggle with wage costs and sub-1.5x solvency; capital infusion, merger or repricing possible.

Accounting and regulatory transition: Ind AS 117, RBC solvency, 100% FDI and Bima Sugam raise comparability, capital efficiency and competition over FY27-29; reported metrics (IGAAP vs Ind AS) will be noisy.
